argon.mechanism: Information assistance and simulated cyber execution can improve while physical prerequisites, deployment safeguards and response remain separate. Code generation is only one component of development speed.
argon.conditions: Read relevant original report sections 3.2.1.3, 3.2.2.3–5, 3.3.2, 3.4.2–5; visually checked Tables 3.2–3.3 and Figures 3.2 and 3.13. Capability tasks omit external safeguards; oversight evidence distinguishes inline and retrospective monitoring.
argon.counterexample: One of three information comparisons is lower than web baselines; two simulated cyber tasks use unintended solutions. More AI-written code coexists with a nonsignificant capability-trend slope change. Monitoring can miss uncovered surfaces.
argon.evidence: Eight experts rate three information scenarios; twelve cyber challenges are solved at least once. Internal workflow survey covers twelve leaders/researchers. Ten thousand stratified-random training rollouts supplement selected flagged cases in a separate analysis.
argon.limits: Developer report, including commissioned evaluations, without independent revalidation here. No novice physical execution, ordinary-use one-shot success or universal monitor coverage is established. The R&D trend is one metric and period, not a null effect for all AI assistance.
argon.mitigation: Retain explicit requirements for access controls, complete monitoring coverage, tamper resistance and timely intervention. Do not equate a monitor using a separate model with tested resistance to collusive misses.
argon.readerContext: Read M2b1, M2c1, C3a3 and R2 in both editions, including their preceding definitions and following conditions. Explain information versus execution and partial automation versus whole-process progress before presenting statistics.
argon.whyHere: Add four bounded evidence cards and relevant node prose. Update the M2b1 and R2 summaries while retaining existing evidence categories; no source demonstrates the complete harmful or self-improving pathway.

primary.support: Expert informational ratings, unintended cyber solutions, monitoring assumptions, human involvement and bounded R&D trend.

defense.mechanism: Restrictions and detection can reduce extraction used to train imitating models, without directly measuring resulting capabilities, access elsewhere or downstream harm.
defense.conditions: Read the October 12 original methods, provider-platform observation and concluding limitations. The reported quantity is estimated reasoning-token extraction before and after measures; complete windows and denominators are not public.
defense.counterexample: An extractor may use another provider, adapt over time or remain undetected. Reducing output volume need not reduce copied capability or harm by the same proportion.
defense.evidence: Anthropic reports a 10–100-fold reduction on its own platform. Treat this as a developer observation of a defense, not an independent trial or a containment rate.
defense.limits: Durability, sophisticated persistent attackers, substitution and legitimate-user costs remain unresolved. Attribution in the original is a provider assessment, not independently established here.
defense.mitigation: Compare defenses on consistent denominators and track substitution, false positives and later harm. Preserve M3 as a condition requiring failed prevention, detection, containment or recovery at the relevant scale.
defense.readerContext: Read M3 and its misuse tour in Japanese and English. The paragraph first identifies what was reduced, then separates that from the real harm the surrounding pathway discusses.
defense.whyHere: Record positive defense evidence alongside failures so M3 does not imply inevitable defensive defeat. The report does not warrant changing its category or the M3-H joint connection.

primary.locator: Our new methods; How well our new methods work; concluding limitations
primary.support: Provider-observed extraction reduction and explicit durability/substitution uncertainty.

research.mechanism: AI can help produce research artifacts while people still select questions, detect errors and validate results. Withdrawals alter artifact counts without proving that all remaining results are right or wrong.
research.conditions: Read the summer-2026 astronomy case published October 8 and the mathematics README/history pinned to October 8 commit 3014888. Distinguish October 7 history heading, October 8 commit and October 6 original release.
research.counterexample: Two agent reviews missed a calibration error found by a human. A sign error invalidated a mathematical argument and dependent manuscripts. Predicted sky regions are not newly observed data.
research.evidence: The astronomy case uses historical observations plus predictions for the unobserved third. Mathematics withdrawals reduce 722 manuscripts to 719; revised formalization coverage is 300 top-line results, not 300 independently certified discoveries.
research.limits: Exact Claude Science model version and some experiment dates are unspecified. Selected cases lack an unattended-success denominator or a whole-process speed comparison. Individual mathematical proofs were not rerun.
research.mitigation: Keep human and independent review, versioned correction histories and verification costs in productivity claims. Formal proof artifacts and the novelty or importance of the mathematics require distinct checks.
research.readerContext: Read R1, its tour, source/card fields and the research-news contexts in both languages. Existing text introduces formalization and distinguishes research components before the new verification examples.
research.whyHere: R1 was due and these originals materially update its evidence. Add a human-review case, update the existing mathematical card and add a pinned correction source without overwriting earlier review snapshots.

auditors.mechanism: Training an AI investigator can improve discovery and reporting on prepared failures; a reward that favors alarming conclusions can instead promote false findings.
auditors.conditions: Read the v1 paper sections 2–4 and 6 and Appendix G. Haiku 4.5 investigates largely prompt-planted behaviors with held-out behaviors/scenarios, separate training/evaluation judges and selected fine-tuned-target transfer.
auditors.counterexample: Simpler alarming-report rewards produce unsupported claims. Matching a composite does not match every discovery metric. Naturally arising unknown failures may differ from planted ones.
auditors.evidence: Pairwise comparisons and benign targets improve the selected metrics; four dimensions are AI-judged with no human validation. The October 15 author blog points to an August 26 paper, not a new publication date for the experiment.
auditors.limits: One trained base model and short investigations, evaluator-model biases and limited realism constrain generalization. No deployment safety or incident-reduction effect is demonstrated.
auditors.mitigation: Use benign controls, independent judgment, behavior held out from training and representative deployment tests. Preserve verification independent of the researcher AI and check effects after implementation.
auditors.readerContext: R4 explains what safety research does before discussing trained auditors. Both editions distinguish improved checks from guarantees that every unknown failure will be found.
auditors.whyHere: Add positive safety-research evidence with reward failures beside it. Keep R4 tested and its outgoing mitigation conditional on deployed, persistent effects.

primary.support: Training design, benign targets, reward-induced fabrication, AI-judge limits and selected transfer.

external.mechanism: Earlier access to development records can reveal issues final-model testing misses, but access rights alone do not demonstrate detection quality or prevention.
external.conditions: Read the October 15 access/publication terms and same-day SecureBio clarification. Six METR staff receive employee-like access with exclusions; publication needs no approval but predefined redactions remain possible.
external.counterexample: Other partners do not necessarily have the same rights. SecureBio is not yet an identical embedded arrangement. More testing material can still be mislabeled or fail to represent unknown failures.
external.evidence: Replace the older proposal paragraph with the reported access implementation. Reread LASER sampling and lie-detection transfer limits for due C3a1; neither changes the distinction between sampling efficiency, label correctness and coverage.
external.limits: This is the evaluated company’s account, not an evaluator’s impact assessment. Do not claim measured reduction in misses or incidents, or that one fine-tuning method generalizes to all types of dishonesty.
external.mitigation: Check access denied, publication constraints and response authority alongside test coverage. Evaluate monitoring models on unfamiliar failure types and seek independent validation of labels.
external.readerContext: Read C3a1 and the evaluation context in Japanese and English. The text explains the coverage problem first, then describes institutional access as one candidate improvement.
external.whyHere: C3a1 was due. Update this substantive access change and its source/card while retaining technical explanations and the indirect category; refresh only its node/evidence dates.

timehorizon.mechanism: Task-completion horizons express human-expert task difficulty at fixed AI success rates; job automation and unattended runtime require different measurements.
timehorizon.conditions: Reread METR methods/FAQ and change history, and the original eleven-task Ironclad evaluation. The horizon page last lists added measurements on May 8 and clarifies discontinued active maintenance on September 8.
timehorizon.counterexample: Partial-credit workflow scores can improve without more jobs being fully completed. Selected software tasks may omit tacit knowledge, interpersonal coordination and exceptions.
timehorizon.evidence: METR uses 50%/80% success horizons and warns about values above sixteen hours. Ironclad reports 55.0% versus 41.6% rubric scores, with estimated time savings and unmatched reasoning settings.
timehorizon.limits: No measured customer time saving, matched-compute causal comparison or universal-task capability follows. A page maintenance notice is not a new measurement or present-day capability ceiling.
timehorizon.mitigation: Keep fixed success criteria, permissions, human intervention and representative tasks. Match actual work before expanding delegated authority.
timehorizon.readerContext: Read C2a and connected capability/automation contexts in both languages. The definition already prevents the runtime confusion; source/card metadata now distinguishes measurement addition from page maintenance.
timehorizon.whyHere: Retain the due C2a explanation and update its node/evidence dates. Correct horizon metadata after substantive rereading, including its source checked date, without dating all downstream nodes anew.

connections.mechanism: Capability, useful research, permissions, safety effectiveness and propagation to harm remain distinct conditional or joint links. Component improvements can coexist with bottlenecks and successful defenses.
connections.conditions: Read thirteen affected edge objects and both translations: M3-H, R1-R2, R2-R3, R3-R2, R4-C1, R0-C2a, R0-R4, C3-L, W1-W4, W4-P1, W4-W3, R0-W1 and R0-ASI.
connections.counterexample: More code may not speed experiments or verification. A simulated task does not grant deployment access. Detection need not trigger timely interruption. Technical ability may not cause adoption, lower prices or universal job substitution.
connections.evidence: New originals describe narrower components and defenses than the full transitions. The R&D trend and mathematics corrections reinforce existing caveats; no complete harmful or unlimited-feedback chain is demonstrated.
connections.limits: Do not compose observations from different models and environments into a verified AND path. New source metadata does not provide new evidence for macroeconomic outcomes or ASI.
connections.mitigation: Preserve conditions for independent checking, deployed safeguards, controlled access, containment and recovery. Retain social and cost conditions for adoption and distribution.
connections.readerContext: Read the edge labels together with current evidence, conditions, limitations and safeguards in both languages. Their plain-language conditional wording remains compatible with the updated nodes.
connections.whyHere: Endpoint/source changes invalidate fingerprints even without an edge edit. Retain all thirteen texts, relations and dates after checking the implications rather than automatically certifying arrows from model scores.

context.counterexample: Better research or monitoring does not prove safety; selected failures do not establish extinction. Historical software measurements and new robot demos do not show all labor can be replaced or that everyone receives the gains.

context.limits: This dependency reading is not a new scientific audit of every historical source or a refresh of every item date. Graph and route fingerprints propagate from narrower source edits.

provenance.counterexample: A blog discovery date does not republish an August paper. A September maintenance notice does not create new measurements. Index visits and passing builds cannot refresh scientific conclusions.
provenance.evidence: Six new sources, eight new cards, two revised source/cards, eight changed bilingual explanations and three due-item rereviews. Retain all thirty-five earlier history entries/translations, categories and topology.
provenance.limits: Bounded search, not exhaustive detection of silent corrections. No individual proof rerun, independent evaluator-data replication, robot-video audit, browser layout or public-production verification is claimed.
